meta.source: Compiled from ASPCA, AAHA, WSAVA, FDA, PetMD, Vetic India, Zigly, BuraqPets, iAdopt India, GoelVetPharma
meta.disclaimer: This information is for general guidance only. Always consult a licensed veterinarian for medical decisions.

diet.disclaimer: Dietary needs vary by individual pet. Consult your vet before making significant diet changes.

puppy.label: Puppy (0–12 months)
puppy.description: Puppies need twice the calories per kilogram as adult dogs. High protein and DHA for brain and eye development are critical.
puppy.indianHomeFood: Boiled chicken + white rice + cooked carrot. No salt, no spices. Max 30% of total diet.
puppy.waterIntake: Approximately 1ml per kcal of food consumed. Always keep fresh water available.

weatherTips.summer: Increase water by 20%. Feed early morning and late evening to avoid heat-induced nausea.
weatherTips.monsoon: Avoid raw food to prevent fungal/bacterial infection. Store dry kibble in airtight containers.
weatherTips.winter: Slightly increase caloric intake for outdoor dogs. Warm up wet food slightly.

adult.label: Adult (1–7 years)
adult.description: Balanced maintenance diet. Protein and fat requirements stabilise. Adjust for activity level.
recommended: Heads Up for Tails fresh food (subscription)
adult.indianHomeFood: Boiled chicken/fish + rice + cooked vegetables (carrot, pumpkin, sweet potato). No onion, garlic, salt.
adult.waterIntake: 50ml per kg body weight daily minimum.

weatherTips.summer: Feed during cooler parts of day. Increase hydration. Watch for heatstroke signs.
weatherTips.monsoon: Keep food fresh. Anti-parasite treatment recommended.
weatherTips.winter: Active outdoor dogs may need 10–15% more calories.

senior.label: Senior (7+ years)
senior.description: Senior dogs need maintained or increased protein to prevent muscle wasting. Reduce phosphorus if kidney issues present.
senior.proteinPercent: 18–25% (do not reduce unless kidney disease confirmed)
recommended: Wet food if dental issues present
avoid: High phosphorus food if kidney disease
Hard kibble without soaking if dental pain
senior.indianHomeFood: Soft boiled chicken + rice + cooked sweet potato. Easier to chew. No bones.
senior.waterIntake: Senior dogs are prone to dehydration. Encourage water with wet food or broth addition.

weatherTips.summer: Very vulnerable to heat. Keep indoors during peak heat hours.
weatherTips.winter: Senior joints worsen in cold. Provide warm bedding. Slightly warmer food.

breedNotes.Labrador Retriever: Prone to obesity. Measure portions carefully. Avoid free feeding.
breedNotes.German Shepherd: Prone to bloat — feed 2 meals not 1 large meal. Avoid exercise immediately after eating.
breedNotes.Pomeranian: Small stomach. 3 small meals better than 2 large. Toy-breed formulas recommended.
breedNotes.Indie/Mixed Breed: Generally hardy digestive system. Mid-range protein formula works well.
breedNotes.Pug: Brachycephalic — smaller kibble or wet food. Prone to obesity. Monitor portions closely.
breedNotes.Golden Retriever: Joint-supportive diet with glucosamine from age 3+. Moderate calorie control.

kitten.label: Kitten (0–12 months)
kitten.description: Kittens need nearly 3x the energy of adult cats. High protein including taurine is mandatory for heart health.
kitten.taurineNote: Cats CANNOT synthesise taurine. It must be in their diet. Deficiency causes heart disease and blindness.

weatherTips.summer: Kittens dehydrate quickly. Wet food preferred. Multiple small water bowls.
weatherTips.monsoon: Keep strictly indoor to avoid leptospirosis and parvo exposure.
weatherTips.winter: Keep warm. Kittens cannot regulate temperature well.

adult.label: Adult (1–7 years)
adult.description: Obligate carnivore diet. Cats need animal-based protein. Do not feed grain-free without vet guidance.
adult.indianHomeFood: Boiled boneless chicken + minimal rice. No spices. Occasional canned tuna in water only.

weatherTips.summer: Indoor cats: keep air circulated. Ensure hydration. Wet food helps.
weatherTips.monsoon: Watch for upper respiratory infections common in humid conditions.
weatherTips.winter: Indoor cats may reduce activity — reduce portions slightly to avoid weight gain.

senior.label: Senior (7+ years)
senior.description: Senior cats actually need MORE protein to prevent muscle wasting — contrary to popular belief.
avoid: Low protein senior foods unless kidney disease confirmed
Hard dry food if dental pain

breedNotes.Persian: Flat face — smaller kibble. Prone to kidney disease. Higher water intake critical.
breedNotes.Siamese: High energy — needs calorie-dense food. Very vocal when hungry.
breedNotes.Bengal: Active breed — higher caloric needs. Raw diet enthusiasts but ensure vet guidance.
breedNotes.Indie/Mixed Breed: Generally robust. Standard adult cat food works well.

general.label: Pet Birds
general.description: Bird diet varies significantly by species. Seed-only diets are nutritionally deficient.
general.keyPrinciple: Seeds should be maximum 50% of diet. Fresh vegetables, fruits, and pellets are essential.
general.waterNote: Change water twice daily. Bird water bowls contaminate quickly.

weatherTips.summer: Provide misting. Keep cage in ventilated shade. Provide fresh water every 4 hours.
weatherTips.monsoon: Watch for fungal growth in food. Clean cage daily in humid weather.
weatherTips.winter: Birds are tropical — maintain temperature above 18°C. Cover cage at night.

general.keyPrinciple: Overfeeding is the #1 cause of fish death. Feed only what fish consume in 2–3 minutes.

Goldfish.diet: Goldfish pellets/flakes, blanched peas (digestion aid), blanched zucchini, occasional bloodworms
Goldfish.avoid: Bread, crackers, high-protein food designed for tropical fish

Betta.diet: Betta-specific pellets, frozen/live bloodworms, daphnia, brine shrimp

Koi.diet: Koi pellets, wheat germ pellets (spring/autumn), spirulina, fresh peas, watermelon
Koi.frequency: 3–4x daily in summer, 1x in cold (under 10°C stop feeding)

Discus.diet: Discus-specific pellets, frozen bloodworms, beef heart (occasional), beefheart-based food
Discus.note: Discus are sensitive — water quality is nutrition. 30% water change every 2 days.

Bearded Dragon.recommended: Collard greens, mustard greens, butternut squash, crickets, dubia roaches
Bearded Dragon.avoid: Iceberg lettuce, avocado, fireflies (toxic), spinach (binds calcium)
Bearded Dragon.supplements: Calcium powder on every feeding. Vitamin D3 3x/week.
Bearded Dragon.uvb: UVB light 10–12 hours/day. Critical for calcium metabolism.

Indian Star Tortoise.diet: Grasses (primary), dark leafy greens, hibiscus flowers, cactus pad
Indian Star Tortoise.avoid: Fruits (too high sugar), animal protein, commercial pellets with preservatives
Indian Star Tortoise.note: Grazing animal — access to grass is ideal. Overfeeding causes pyramid shell.

Leopard Gecko.diet: Exclusively insects: crickets, dubia roaches, mealworms, waxworms (occasional treat)
Leopard Gecko.avoid: Any plant material, fruits, vegetables (insectivore only)
Leopard Gecko.supplements: Calcium in dish always available. Vitamin D3 2x/week.

Guinea Pig.diet: Unlimited timothy hay (critical), fresh vegetables (bell pepper, leafy greens), guinea pig pellets
Guinea Pig.vitaminC: Cannot synthesise Vitamin C. Must come from diet. Bell pepper is best source.
Guinea Pig.avoid: Iceberg lettuce, potatoes, onion, garlic, rhubarb, dairy
Guinea Pig.note: Hay must be 80% of diet. Gut motility depends on constant fibre.

Holland Lop Rabbit.diet: Unlimited timothy hay, fresh leafy greens, limited pellets (1/4 cup per 2kg body weight)
Holland Lop Rabbit.avoid: Iceberg lettuce, cabbage, nuts, seeds, bread, pasta, chocolate
Holland Lop Rabbit.note: Like guinea pigs — gut stasis (digestive shutdown) is life-threatening. Hay is non-negotiable.

Hamster.diet: Hamster seed mix, fresh vegetables (broccoli, carrot), occasional hard-boiled egg
Hamster.avoid: Citrus fruits, onion, garlic, almonds, apple seeds
Hamster.note: Hamsters cache food. Check and clean food stores weekly to prevent mold.

illness.disclaimer: ⚠️ This is general guidance only. These are NOT a substitute for veterinary diagnosis. If symptoms are severe, persistent, or your pet is very young/very old, seek immediate vet care.

Vomiting.description: Common in both dogs and cats. Often resolves in 24 hours.
Vomiting.whenToWorry: Vomiting more than 3 times/hour, blood in vomit, lethargy, distended belly, foreign object suspected
homeRemedies: Fast for 12–24 hours (water only) for dogs. 8–12 hours for cats.
After fasting: bland diet — boiled plain chicken + white rice in small amounts every 2–3 hours
Ensure access to fresh water to prevent dehydration
Avoid normal food for 48 hours post-vomiting
Vomiting.vetRequired: If vomiting continues beyond 24 hours, blood present, or accompanied by diarrhoea and lethargy
Vomiting.indiaNote: In hot weather, vomiting may indicate heatstroke — move pet to cool area immediately.

Diarrhoea.description: Loose or watery stools. Often dietary or stress-related.
homeRemedies: Bland diet: boiled chicken + white rice for 2–3 days
For cats: ensure taurine is still in diet if home cooking
Probiotics (pet-specific) can help restore gut flora
Pumpkin puree (plain, no spice) — 1 teaspoon for small dogs — adds fibre
Diarrhoea.vetRequired: Blood in stool, more than 24 hours, lethargy, dehydration signs (sunken eyes, dry gums), in puppies/kittens
Diarrhoea.indiaNote: Parvo is common in unvaccinated puppies in India. Diarrhoea in puppies = vet immediately.

Itching/Skin Issues.description: Scratching, hot spots, redness. Common causes: fleas, food allergy, contact allergy, fungal infection.
homeRemedies: Oatmeal bath: grind oats into fine powder, mix in warm water, soak 10–15 minutes
Coconut oil: apply topically to dry/itchy areas. Antimicrobial and moisturising.
Check for fleas: use flea comb. Look for black pepper-like specks (flea dirt).
Anti-flea treatment: Spot-on treatments like Frontline, Bravecto, or Advocate (vet recommended)
Itching/Skin Issues.vetRequired: Open wounds, loss of fur in patches, infection signs (smell, discharge), no improvement in 5 days

Fever.description: Normal dog temp: 38–39.2°C. Normal cat temp: 38–39.2°C. Above 39.5°C is fever.
Fever.howToCheck: Rectal thermometer is most accurate. Ear thermometers available too.
homeRemedies: Cool (not cold) damp cloth on paw pads and armpits
Ensure hydration — encourage drinking
Keep pet in cool, ventilated area
Monitor every 30 minutes
Fever.vetRequired: Temperature above 40°C, fever lasting more than 24 hours, accompanied by vomiting/lethargy/seizures
Fever.warning: Never give human paracetamol/panadol — FATAL to both dogs and cats.

Worms/Parasites.description: Roundworms, hookworms, tapeworms, whipworms common in India. Visible signs: pot belly in puppies, worms in stool, weight loss, dull coat.
homeRemedies: No effective home remedy for worms — deworming medication required
Keep environment clean — pick up stools promptly
Wash bedding regularly in hot water
Worms/Parasites.treatment: Deworming medications: Drontal (dogs), Milbemax, Panacur. Available at vet clinics. Puppy schedule: every 2 weeks until 3 months, then monthly until 6 months, then every 3 months.
Worms/Parasites.vetRequired: Always use vet-prescribed dewormer. Dose depends on body weight.

Respiratory Infection.description: Birds hide illness until critical. Fluffed feathers, tail bobbing while breathing, nasal discharge, clicking sounds = respiratory issue.
homeRemedies: Keep bird warm (28–30°C)
Remove drafts completely
Ensure fresh, clean water
Isolate from other birds immediately
Respiratory Infection.vetRequired: ANY respiratory symptoms in birds = vet immediately. Birds deteriorate rapidly.

Appetite Loss.description: Not eating for 12–24 hours can indicate anything from stress to serious illness.
homeRemedies: Warm food slightly to enhance aroma
Try offering different texture (wet vs dry)
Ensure fresh water is available
Check for dental pain — difficulty chewing can cause appetite loss
Reduce stress sources: new pets, moving, visitors
Appetite Loss.vetRequired: Not eating for more than 24 hours in adult dogs, 12 hours in cats or birds, any time in puppies/kittens

training.disclaimer: Training requires patience and consistency. Never use punishment-based methods. Positive reinforcement is most effective and humane.

spaceLarge.label: Large space (house with large garden or access to park)

day1.morning: Name recognition: say name + treat reward 20 times. Charge the clicker if using one.
day1.evening: Sit: lure nose up with treat, say 'Sit', reward. 5–10 repetitions.

day2.morning: Sit revision (5 mins) + Down: lure treat to ground, say 'Down', reward.
day2.evening: Sit + Down practice. Name recognition game.

day3.morning: Sit, Down revision + Stay: ask for Sit, say 'Stay', take 1 step back, return and treat.
day3.evening: Increase Stay to 3 steps back. Multiple repetitions.

day4.morning: Recall: call name + 'Come', run backward excitedly, reward with jackpot treat on arrival.
day4.evening: Practice Sit + Down + Stay + Come in sequence.

day5.morning: Loose leash walking: 10-minute walk, stop every time leash tightens. Resume when loose.
day5.evening: Sit, Down, Stay, Come review. Add 'Off' if jumping is an issue.

day6.morning: All commands review in new location (different room or outside).
day6.evening: Rest and play session. Mental enrichment (sniff game with hidden treats).

day7.morning: Assessment day: test all 5 commands (Sit, Down, Stay, Come, loose leash).
day7.evening: Free play and bonding. No formal training.

day8.morning: Impulse control: 'Leave it' — place treat on floor, cover with hand, say 'Leave it', reward.
day8.evening: Leave it with treat on ground uncovered.

day9.morning: Place command: teach dog to go to their bed/mat and stay.

day10.morning: Leash manners in outdoor environment. Practice heel.
day10.evening: Recall in garden or open space. Increase distance.

day11.morning: Door manners: sit before door opens. Reinforce calm greetings.
day11.evening: Leave it with food bowl: dog must wait for release cue.

day12.evening: Mental enrichment: food puzzle, sniff games.

day13.morning: Introduction to 'Shake' (paw): hold treat in closed fist, dog paws at hand, open and reward.
day13.evening: Revision of all learned commands in sequence.

day14.evening: Rest day — free play and bonding time.

day15.label: Day 15 — Graduation Assessment
day15.morning: Full command run-through: Sit, Down, Stay (10 sec), Come (5m recall), Loose leash walk, Leave it, Place.
day15.evening: Celebration play session. Continue daily 5–10 min maintenance sessions.
day15.nextSteps: Consider puppy socialization classes, agility introduction, or tricks training.

importantTips: Always end on success — if dog fails, make it easier and end with a win
Puppies (under 12 weeks): max 5 minutes per session
Hot weather: train indoors or early morning/late evening only
Never train a hungry dog to desperation or a completely full dog
Jackpot reward (extra treats + excited praise) for first-time successes
Avoid scolding — it breaks trust and slows learning

Feline.note: Cats can be trained but require shorter sessions and higher-value rewards. Clicker training works well.

sessions.day1: Charge clicker: click + immediately give treat. 20 repetitions twice daily.
sessions.day2: Sit: lure treat over head, click the moment bottom touches ground.
sessions.day4: Target stick: touch stick with nose = click + treat.

sessions.day8: Come when called: call name + clicker + jackpot treat.
sessions.day10: Carrier training: click for any interest in carrier, gradually progress to entering.

poisonPrevention.disclaimer: If you suspect your pet has ingested a toxic substance, contact your vet immediately. Do NOT induce vomiting unless instructed by a vet.

items.name: Chocolate
items.symptoms: Vomiting, diarrhoea, increased heart rate, seizures, death
items.note: Dark chocolate and baking chocolate are most dangerous. Even small amounts can kill small dogs.

items.name: Onion, Garlic, Leek, Chives
items.symptoms: Anaemia (destroys red blood cells), weakness, pale gums, collapse
items.note: Cooked, raw, or powdered — all forms toxic. Garlic is 5x more toxic than onion. Very common in Indian cooking — keep all Indian food away from pets.

items.name: Grapes and Raisins
items.symptoms: Acute kidney failure within 24–48 hours
items.note: Even small amounts can cause fatal kidney failure. Mechanism not fully understood.

items.name: Xylitol (sugar-free sweetener)
items.symptoms: Blood sugar crash (within 30 min), seizures, liver failure
items.note: Found in sugar-free gum, some peanut butters, mouthwash, medications. Check peanut butter labels before giving to dogs.

items.name: Macadamia Nuts
items.symptoms: Weakness, vomiting, tremors, hyperthermia
items.note: Not fatal but causes significant distress. Common in imported biscuits.

items.name: Avocado
items.severity: HIGH for birds, MILD for dogs/cats
items.symptoms: Respiratory distress and death in birds; mild GI upset in dogs/cats
items.note: Fatal to birds and rabbits. Dogs and cats generally tolerate small amounts but best avoided.

items.name: Caffeine (coffee, tea, energy drinks)
items.symptoms: Hyperactivity, tremors, seizures, abnormal heart rhythm

items.name: Alcohol
items.symptoms: Vomiting, disorientation, breathing difficulty, coma, death
items.note: Even small amounts dangerous. Indian sweets with alcohol base — keep away.

items.name: Raw yeast dough
items.symptoms: Bloat (life-threatening gas expansion), alcohol toxicity as yeast ferments

items.name: Salt (excess)
items.symptoms: Vomiting, diarrhoea, seizures (large amounts), excessive thirst
items.note: Namkeen, chips, papad — all too salty for pets. Indian snacks are a common source.

items.name: Milk and dairy (large amounts)
items.symptoms: Diarrhoea, digestive upset
items.note: Most adult pets are lactose intolerant. Small amounts usually fine but not recommended.

items.name: Oleander (Kaner)
items.symptoms: Heart arrhythmia, vomiting, death
items.note: Extremely common ornamental plant in India. All parts including dried leaves toxic.

items.name: Dieffenbachia (Dumb Cane)
items.symptoms: Intense mouth burning, swelling, drooling, difficulty swallowing
items.note: Very common houseplant in India. Keep out of reach.

items.name: Sago Palm (Cycas)
items.symptoms: Vomiting, liver failure, death within days
items.note: One of the most toxic plants. Common in Indian gardens and housing societies.

items.name: Lilies (all varieties)
items.symptoms: Kidney failure and death in cats. Even pollen can be fatal.
items.note: Easter lily, tiger lily, peace lily — all deadly to cats. Keep all lilies out of homes with cats.

items.name: Euphorbia (Spurge family)
items.symptoms: Skin irritation, mouth burning, vomiting
items.note: Milky sap of euphorbias (common succulents and croton) toxic on contact.

items.name: Aloe Vera
items.symptoms: Vomiting, diarrhoea, lethargy
items.note: Gel is safe topically but toxic if ingested.

items.name: Tulsi (Holy Basil)
items.symptoms: GI upset in cats
items.note: Tulsi is safe for dogs in very small amounts. Cats more sensitive — avoid.

items.name: Hibiscus
items.symptoms: Anorexia, diarrhoea
items.note: Safe for dogs and cats but avoid for small pets.

items.name: Castor bean (Arandi)
items.symptoms: Severe vomiting, dehydration, tremors, seizures, death
items.note: Common weed in India. Seeds extremely toxic.

items.name: Rat poison (rodenticides)
items.symptoms: Internal bleeding, seizures, death
items.note: Brodifacoum-based rat poisons common in India. Pets exposed by eating poisoned rodents too.

items.name: Human medications
items.note: Never give human medication to pets. Paracetamol causes fatal liver failure in cats.

items.name: Insecticides/Pesticides
items.note: Organophosphate pesticides (common in India) extremely dangerous. Keep pets away during spraying.

items.name: Essential oils
items.symptoms: Liver failure, respiratory distress
items.note: Tea tree oil, eucalyptus, lavender — concentrated essential oils toxic to cats. Avoid diffusers in rooms where cats rest.

items.name: Diwali fireworks
items.note: Chemical ingestion from spent fireworks toxic. Keep pets indoors during Diwali, away from firecrackers.

carTravel.label: Car Travel Safety
tips: Never leave pets in a parked car — temperatures can reach 60°C+ in Indian summers within minutes
Use a secured carrier or dog seatbelt harness — unrestrained pets can become projectiles in accidents
Place carrier on floor of back seat — safest position in a crash
Crack windows for ventilation but not enough for pet to escape
Never let dog hang head out of window — eye/ear injuries from debris common
Bring water and collapsible bowl for journeys over 1 hour
Stop every 2–3 hours for toilet break and stretch
Feed a light meal 3–4 hours before travel to reduce motion sickness
For anxious pets: vet can prescribe anti-anxiety medication or motion sickness tablets
ID tag on collar + microchip essential when travelling away from home

withKids.label: Pet Safety with Children
rules: Never leave dogs and young children unsupervised — even the most gentle dog can bite when startled
Teach children to ask before petting any dog — including family pets when eating or sleeping
Do not disturb a dog while eating, sleeping, or caring for puppies
Teach 'be a tree' if dog approaches aggressively: stand still, arms folded, look away
Children should not take food from dogs or disturb their food bowl
Warn children: do not run from or scream at dogs — triggers chase instinct
Cats: teach children to let cat approach first, never pick up unwillingly
All children should wash hands after handling pets

homeSafety.label: Home Safety for Pets
tips: Secure all medications in closed cabinets — common cause of pet poisoning
Keep toilet lid closed — small pets can fall in and drown
Secure loose electrical wires — puppies and kittens chew wires and risk electrocution
Block balcony gaps — cats especially can fall from great heights
Remove toxic houseplants (see Poison Prevention section)
Keep washing machine and dryer doors closed — cats sleep inside
Secure garbage bins — food waste access causes illness
Store cleaning chemicals in locked or high cupboards
Check under car before reversing — cats shelter under vehicles
Ensure garden fencing is secure and free of gaps for small dogs

eldersSafety.label: Pet Safety Around Elderly People
tips: Large dogs can knock over elderly individuals — train 'four paws on floor' command
Ensure pet toys and bowls are not on stairs or walkways — tripping hazards
Choose calmer breeds for elderly owners — not high-energy working dogs
Retractable leashes are a fall risk for elderly walkers — use fixed-length leash
Elderly owners: arrange pet care backup plan for health emergencies
Cats on laps/beds can be a fall risk when getting up — train pet off furniture if needed

pregnantPet.label: Pregnant Pet Safety
tips: Confirm pregnancy with vet via ultrasound at 3–4 weeks post-mating
Increase food by 25–50% in last 3 weeks of pregnancy
Provide a quiet, private nesting area 1 week before due date
Do not vaccinate or deworm during pregnancy — consult vet for safe alternatives
Avoid stressful situations, loud environments, introduction of new animals
Normal gestation: dogs 63 days, cats 65–67 days, rabbits 28–32 days
Signs of labour: restlessness, nesting, panting, loss of appetite
Emergency signs: labour lasting more than 2 hours with no birth, greenish discharge without birth, kitten/puppy stuck in birth canal

weatherSafety.label: Weather Safety for Pets in India

summer.label: Summer Safety (March–June)
tips: Walk dogs before 8am and after 7pm — tarmac above 30°C burns paw pads
Test tarmac: press back of hand on ground for 5 seconds — if too hot for you, too hot for paws
Ensure shade and water access at all times outdoors
Signs of heatstroke: heavy panting, drooling, staggering, collapse — wet dog with cool (not cold) water and rush to vet
Brachycephalic breeds (Pug, Shih Tzu, Persian cat) at extreme risk — keep air-conditioned
Never leave pets in cars even with windows cracked

monsoon.label: Monsoon Safety (June–September)
tips: Leptospirosis spread through flood water — vaccinate dogs annually (Lepto vaccine)
Dry pets thoroughly after rain — ear infections and skin fungus common
Check paws after walks — cuts and infections from debris in water
Ticks and fleas peak in monsoon — monthly anti-parasitic treatment essential
Thunderstorm anxiety: create a safe den, consult vet about anti-anxiety options
Avoid puddles and stagnant water on walks — contaminated with pathogens

winter.label: Winter Safety (November–February)
tips: Short-coated breeds (Doberman, Indie dogs) feel cold below 10°C — provide sweater/indoor shelter
Senior and young pets lose body heat faster — extra bedding required
Antifreeze (ethylene glycol) has sweet taste and is FATAL — keep away from pets
Reduced daylight — use reflective collar/leash for evening walks
Arthritis worsens in cold — older pets may need pain management from vet
Indoor birds: maintain temperature above 18°C at night

firstAid.label: Pet First Aid Essentials
kitContents: Gauze bandages and adhesive bandages (not human bandaids)
Hydrogen peroxide 3% (ONLY if vet instructs vomiting induction)
Muzzle or soft cloth strip (injured animals may bite from pain)

basicProcedures.action: Apply firm pressure with gauze for 5–10 minutes. Do not remove pad if soaking through — add more gauze on top. Rush to vet if arterial bleeding.
Do not attempt to splint. Keep pet still and calm. Support body when lifting. Transport to vet immediately.
Cool with room-temperature water for 20 minutes. Do NOT use ice or butter. Cover loosely with clean cloth. Vet immediately.
Look in mouth if safe to do so. Do not blindly finger-sweep. For dogs: modified Heimlich — firm pressure behind ribcage. Rush to vet.
Move to shade/AC immediately. Wet with cool (not cold) water. Fan the pet. Do not cover. Rush to vet. This is a life-threatening emergency.

foodSafety.label: Food Safety for Pets
tips: Never feed table scraps containing onion, garlic, chili, masalas — toxic
Wash food and water bowls daily — bacteria grow rapidly in India's climate
Dry kibble: store in airtight container, away from moisture
Wet food: refrigerate after opening, discard after 24 hours
Treats: should be max 10% of daily caloric intake
Check expiry dates on pet food — particularly important in Indian summer storage
Do not feed bones from chicken, fish, pork — splintering causes internal injuries

biteSafety.label: Pet Bite Safety
forOwners: Clean bite wound immediately with soap and water for 5 minutes
Seek medical attention — even minor dog bites carry infection risk
Report stray dog bites to local authority and get anti-rabies prophylaxis (PEP) immediately
Do not delay PEP — rabies is 100% fatal once symptoms appear
preventingBites: Never approach a dog that is eating, sleeping or with puppies
Do not make direct eye contact with an unfamiliar dog
Be a tree: stand still, arms folded, look away if a dog approaches aggressively
Never run from an aggressive dog — triggers chase instinct
Teach children bite safety rules from an early age

dogs: Monthly: spot-on flea/tick treatment (Frontline Plus, Bravecto, Nexgard, Simparica)
Every 6 months: heartworm test (especially in monsoon-heavy regions)
Annually: full health checkup including fecal test
cats: Every 3 months: deworming (Milbemax cat, Drontal cat — different from dog formula)
Never: use dog flea products on cats — permethrin in dog products is FATAL to cats

commonParasites.name: Ticks
commonParasites.risk: Transmit tick fever, ehrlichiosis, babesiosis — all potentially fatal
commonParasites.action: Remove with tweezers — grip close to skin, pull straight up. Do not twist. Crush body spreads disease. Use tick-prevention products monthly.

commonParasites.name: Fleas
commonParasites.risk: Cause intense itching, anaemia in young pets, tapeworm transmission
commonParasites.action: Treat pet AND home environment simultaneously. Wash bedding in hot water. Treat all pets in household.

commonParasites.name: Heartworm
commonParasites.risk: Mosquito-transmitted. Often fatal if untreated. Higher risk in humid regions of India.
commonParasites.action: Prevention far easier than treatment. Monthly preventive medication essential.
